title: Microinteraction Design Patterns — States, Contextual Interaction and Motion Polish
scope: General product-independent UI/UX; desktop, web, keyboard and touch.

patterns.name: Hover State / Hover Highlight
patterns.behavior: Pointer over an interactive target; distinguish from persistent selection.
patterns.acceptance: Visual feedback changes only relevant affordance; mouseout restores prior state; no hover-only access.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Pressed State
patterns.behavior: Transient press feedback distinct from toggle's persistent pressed semantics.
patterns.acceptance: Pointer down/up and keyboard activation work; cancel press when appropriate; no layout shift.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Focus Visible
patterns.behavior: Visible keyboard focus, not merely pointer hover.
patterns.acceptance: Tab through controls; focus is visible and not obscured; avoid removing outline without replacement.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Focus Within
patterns.behavior: Highlight parent or reveal actions when a descendant receives focus.
patterns.acceptance: Move focus among actions; row remains usable until focus leaves; no keyboard-only disappearing controls.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Selected State
patterns.behavior: Persistent selection separate from hover, focus and current destination.
patterns.acceptance: Selection survives pointer movement; accessible semantics fit actual widget; combine states coherently.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Disabled State
patterns.behavior: Communicate unavailable action and reason where useful; use actual semantics.
patterns.acceptance: Disabled action cannot accidentally execute; explain missing prerequisites accessibly.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Loading / Busy State
patterns.behavior: Represent ongoing work without implying success or blocking unrelated actions.
patterns.acceptance: Loading and completion match actual work; screen reader receives relevant updates; failure recoverable.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Dragging State
patterns.behavior: Show held item, original position and relevant drag feedback.
patterns.acceptance: Drag cancel restores state; touch/keyboard and single-pointer alternative available.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Drop Target / Insertion Indicator
patterns.behavior: Distinguish valid target and insertion position; do not rely only on color.
patterns.acceptance: Valid and invalid drop targets clear; no accidental reorder; alternative move command works.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: State Layers
patterns.behavior: Compose state-dependent surface or overlay styling for interaction feedback; design-system technique rather than universal requirement.
patterns.acceptance: Selected+hover+focus combination stays legible in light/dark modes.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Hover-Reveal Actions
patterns.behavior: Reveal secondary row controls on pointer intent without hiding essentials.
patterns.acceptance: No row resizing or click interception; move pointer to child action without disappearance.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Focus-Reveal Actions
patterns.behavior: Reveal equivalent controls via keyboard; touch fallback through explicit affordance.
patterns.acceptance: Tab to actions; controls remain visible and operable on touch-only device.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Overflow Menu Trigger / More Actions
patterns.behavior: Use recognizable control to access secondary actions in context.
patterns.acceptance: Accessible name, keyboard open/close, correct item scope, focus return; label ambiguous icons.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Hover Intent
patterns.behavior: Delay or infer intentional hover for secondary surfaces to reduce accidental activation.
patterns.acceptance: Rapid cursor transit doesn't open unwanted panels; deliberate dwell works; no fixed universal delay.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Delayed Tooltip
patterns.behavior: Short noninteractive explanation for a labeled or unfamiliar control; not sole source of essential information.
patterns.acceptance: Pointer/focus opens; Escape dismisses; no interactive controls inside tooltip; preserve accessible name.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Tooltip Delay Group / Skip Delay
patterns.behavior: After deliberate opening, allow faster neighboring tooltips during a bounded group interval.
patterns.acceptance: First opening delayed; adjacent labels appear promptly; delay resets after leaving group; no focus stealing.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Hover Card
patterns.behavior: Contextual preview beyond a brief label; interactive content requires suitable popover/dialog semantics.
patterns.acceptance: Preview can be dismissed; keyboard/touch path; important information accessible without hover.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Interest-Triggered Preview
patterns.behavior: Preview an item before committing navigation; product-specific trigger may be hover, focus or explicit action.
patterns.acceptance: Preview does not change committed selection or navigation; explicit opening path works.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Anchored Popover
patterns.behavior: Position contextual surface relative to its trigger; semantics depend on content.
patterns.acceptance: Scroll/resize keeps anchor relationship; Escape, focus behavior and touch supported.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Safe Polygon / Pointer Travel Corridor
patterns.behavior: Implementation technique to preserve hover surface during intentional pointer travel.
patterns.acceptance: Diagonal movement into menu stays open; moving away closes; no reliance on pointer-only interaction.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Adaptive Placement / Collision Avoidance
patterns.behavior: Flip or shift overlay to remain available near viewport boundaries.
patterns.acceptance: Test edges, scroll, zoom, narrow viewport and content clipping.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Expanded Hit Area
patterns.behavior: Increase operable target around small visual icon while preserving distinct targets.
patterns.acceptance: Test adjacent target overlap, touch and keyboard; apply WCAG target-size criteria and exceptions.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Color Transition
patterns.behavior: Animate changes of visual state when helpful; prioritize instant semantic feedback.
patterns.acceptance: Rapid enter/leave reverses smoothly; contrast and selected/focus distinction remain clear.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Opacity Transition
patterns.behavior: Fade nonessential visuals on state change; distinguish invisible from noninteractive.
patterns.acceptance: Hidden controls don't capture input invisibly; reveal on focus/touch; no delayed essential feedback.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Press Feedback
patterns.behavior: Subtle response to activation; avoid compulsory scaling or movement.
patterns.acceptance: Keyboard and touch receive feedback; reduced-motion alternative retains state cue.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Icon Morphing
patterns.behavior: Transition icon shape for closely related states only if meaning remains obvious.
patterns.acceptance: Accessible name/state update immediately; reduced-motion alternative; no unrelated visual confusion.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Origin-Aware Animation
patterns.behavior: Maintain spatial link from triggering control to resulting surface.
patterns.acceptance: Popover enters/exits from meaningful anchor; works after collision reposition; no animation prerequisite.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Interruptible / Reversible Animation
patterns.behavior: New user input supersedes ongoing transition rather than queues stale motion.
patterns.acceptance: Rapid reopen/close and repeated toggles converge on current state; no delayed input.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Layout Animation
patterns.behavior: Preserve spatial continuity when items add, remove or reorder.
patterns.acceptance: Actual order and focus stay correct; no overlap or blocked interactions.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Shared Element Transition
patterns.behavior: Preserve visible identity between two presentations of same element.
patterns.acceptance: No duplicate accessible objects or stale focus; skip safely when identity or support missing.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Spring Animation
patterns.behavior: Physics-inspired easing for appropriate direct manipulation, not universal motion default.
patterns.acceptance: Tune to task; avoid excessive oscillation; repeated interactions remain responsive.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Enter / Exit Transition
patterns.behavior: Reveal or dismiss contextual surface without interrupting interaction.
patterns.acceptance: Exit doesn't leave hidden focusable controls or intercept input; interruption supported.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

patterns.name: Reduced Motion
patterns.behavior: Respect motion preference and applicable accessibility requirements; preserve meaning.
patterns.acceptance: With reduced motion enabled, all actions, state cues and content remain available.
patterns.priority: contextual; normative accessibility requirements apply independently
patterns.evidence_status: Synthesis of prior research and documented guidance; not a market adoption claim

caveats: Microinteraction Design Patterns, Component Interaction States, Interaction Design Details, UI Craft, Interaction Polish and Design Engineering Guidelines are search terms; the umbrella taxonomy here is a proposed knowledge organization, not a formal universal standard.

Static user screenshot supports an observed row highlight, visible secondary actions and tooltip label, not causation, exact hover trigger, timings, CSS, actual motion or component library; no private image or labels published.

Use a behavior contract: trigger, state before/after, rules, visual feedback, input modality, timing/interruptibility, persistence, accessibility, failure and acceptance. Distinguish observable interaction from implementation choice.

Tooltip is noninteractive explanatory content; an interactive hover card needs appropriate semantics. APG tooltip pattern is still work in progress. WCAG 1.4.13 applies to additional hover/focus content where applicable: dismissible, hoverable and persistent, subject to exceptions. Test touch and keyboard separately.

Do not prescribe a universal duration, delay, scale, opacity or animation for all controls. Use feedback without blocking action; reduced-motion preference must preserve essential cues. State layers and safe polygon are techniques, not formal UX standards.

An outline icon, hidden controls or dark theme is not evidence that an application uses a specific library. Design galleries are existence evidence; examples are not population-level adoption or usability findings.
Cross-reference prior contextual-tool, motion, accessibility and component-behavior catalogs. Counts are indexed entries, not net-new distinct patterns. Preserve original URLs and prior metadata.
